newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada lets fungus-free U.S. durum through Seaway.
newsitem.headline: Canada lets fungus-free U.S. durum through Seaway.

text.p: Agriculture Canada loosened a year-old ban on the transit of U.S. durum wheat through the St. Lawrence Seaway this week, an Ag Canada official said.

"We're now requiring that both bread wheat and durum wheat originating from northern (U.S.) states which have been found to be free of Karnal bunt (fungus) to be tested and certified to be free before they can either enter or be offloaded at Canadian elevators," said Yudi Singh, Agriculture Canada's associate director of plant protection.
Canada on March 29, 1996, barred lake vessels carrying U.S. durum and certain other U.S. wheat from the Seaway.

The fungus, which makes flour smell bad, affects grain yield and quality. It was discovered in March 1996 in parts of California, Arizona, Texas and New Mexico, prompting cancellations by importing nations.
Lake vessels loading grain at U.S. lake ports transfer their cargoes into Canadian terminals between Montreal and Quebec City for loading onto ocean vessels.
Those transfers could leave contaminated kernels in Canadian terminals.
